text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.1% today, recovering most of yesterday's 1.9% drop and reaching its highest price in the two-week span. The rebound follows news that oil prices stabilized after falling sharply on August 26th—when markets initially sold off on reports of a potential Iran-Oman deal to secure safer passage through the Strait of Hormuz, reducing perceived geopolitical risk to crude supplies. With oil prices no longer falling, refiners like Marathon benefit from more predictable input costs and the ability to lock in margins between crude purchases and refined product sales.

The broader context here is ongoing tension around Hormuz, a chokepoint through which roughly a third of the world's seaborne oil passes. While the Iran-Oman discussions suggest a possible de-escalation, the U.S. position remains unsettled, keeping energy markets on edge—exactly the kind of uncertainty that can whipsaw refiner stocks day-to-day as traders weigh whether crude will stay scarce or abundant.
